title: The Human Microbiome
text: The human microbiome refers to the trillions of microorganisms — bacteria, viruses, fungi, and other microbes — that live in and on the human body. The gut microbiome, concentrated in the large intestine, contains approximately 100 trillion microbial cells representing around 1,000 different species. These microbes play crucial roles in digestion, immune system development, and the synthesis of vitamins (K, B12). Disruption of the gut microbiome (dysbiosis) has been linked to conditions including inflammatory bowel disease, obesity, and mental health disorders (the gut-brain axis). The Human Microbiome Project, launched in 2008, aimed to characterize the microbial communities in the human body.
